keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in -1000, but the infobox dates Saul's ascension to c. 1047 BCE and Saul's capital was Gibeah, while David established Judah's capital at Hebron (the page's words, unquoted). The page gives no extent for Saul's or Ish-bosheth's kingdom, so the later northern shape stands for it at confidence 1. Fix 2026-10-19 (reviewer): Gibeah, Saul's capital, lay in the Judah cells removed from this shape, so the Benjamin circle is added back; the Philistine strip cells (8, 35.14-35.52 E, 32.02-33.13 N) that Cliopatria's Philistia -1150 shape also covers are removed and enter at -1000 (gain from philistia).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1000 shape, unchanged, valid for -1000..-931 (Israel and Judah together)

keyframe_review.note: 20,072 km2 (the infobox gives no area): the united monarchy of David and Solomon, reaching east of the Jordan to 36.7 E. The page says Philistia, Moab, Edom and Ammon became client states and Aram-Zobah and Aram-Damascus vassals, which the shape does not include; it calls the biblical portrayal of Solomon's empire 'most probably an anachronistic exaggeration' and records Finkelstein's Low Chronology. The shape stands for -1000..-931 only; after the division (about 930 BCE) Judah is no part of Israel, see the next keyframe. Fix 2026-10-19: the Philistine inland strip inside this shape (11 cells, one of them Gibeah's, held since -1047) joins by the -1000 gain from philistia (10 cells); Jerusalem is the capital from -1000.

New keyframe: after Jeroboam's Revolt (930 BCE in the infobox) the kingdom split into Israel (north, including Shechem and Samaria) and Judah (south, including Jerusalem); Cliopatria keeps one shape to -901 and starts a separate Kingdom of Judah only in -900. The Judah core (2,782 km2, 11 cells) is cut out.

13,747 km2, the northern kingdom: the Samaria page says it controlled Samaria, Galilee and parts of Transjordan. Samaria is the capital from c. 880. The page gives no area. Hazael (842–796) 'conquered Israel' without named lands (Aram-Damascus page) and the Mesha Stele (c. 840) records a Moabite victory; neither is in the shape, so the Transjordan edge is soft. Fix 2026-10-19: the 9 northern coastal cells that Philistia loses at -900 enter this shape by a new -900 gain from philistia (confidence 1).

13,415 km2. Jeroboam II (793–753 or 786–746) extended Israel to its former limits, 'the entering of Hamath to the sea of the plain'; the shape does not reach Hamath, so it draws the core only (unverified beyond that: page budget).

13,415 km2 to -701 is too long: about 732 BCE Tiglath-Pileser III annexed Aram and the Gilead territories of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh and captured Naphtali (Galilee), and Samaria fell in 722 (or c. 720). The shape stands for -750..-733 only; -732..-723 is the rump around Samaria (next keyframe); from -722 there is no Israel.

correction.text: the rump of Israel around Samaria, 732–723

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the annexation of Galilee and Gilead the kingdom is the hill country of Samaria under Hoshea (732–c. 720), Assyria besieged Samaria for three years and Sargon II recorded 'Samaria I looked at, I captured'. The Samaria region (2,782 km2) stands for it. Fix 2026-10-19: Samaria is an Assyrian vassal kingdom here (vassal_start -732, vassal_end -722).

[Fix 2026-10-19: region reduced by the Benjamin circle (held since -1047) and by the Philistia -1150 cells, which the gain from philistia below carries.]
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Philistia becomes a client state. The page says David secured his borders by defeating the Philistines and that Philistia, Moab, Edom and Ammon became client states; no year.
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Moab becomes a client state of David (page: Philistia, Moab, Edom and Ammon became client states; no year).
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Ammon becomes a client state of David; Saul had already led an army to victory over the Ammonites (no year).
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Edom becomes a client state of David (no year on the page).
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Aram-Zobah and Aram-Damascus become vassals of David (page: no year); the Aram-Damascus page places battles between David's Israel and the Arameans in the 10th century BCE.

The united-monarchy page has David 'defeat such regional entities as the Philistines to secure his borders', as the biblical account and with no year; -1000 is Cliopatria's step. Mirrors philistia /ledger/1 (reviewer fix); the cells were inside the first version of the -1047 shape and are now taken out of it.
c. 931 BCE: the northern kingdom's capital is Shechem. Infobox: Shechem (c. 931–909), Tirzah (c. 909–880), Samaria (c. 880–720); Jerusalem stays with Judah.

c. 930 BCE: Jeroboam's Revolt divides the kingdom. The infobox gives Jeroboam's Revolt as 930 BCE and the text says the kingdom split under Rehoboam into Israel (north) and Judah (south); scholars differ on the year.
c. 930 BCE (bridged): the client relation ends with the division; the page gives no date.

c. 909 BCE: the capital moves to Tirzah (infobox: Tirzah c. 909–880).

region.text: the northern Philistine coast, 9 cells, inside Israel's 900 shape

ledger.note: c. 900 BCE (bridged): the northern coast joins Israel. Cliopatria's 900 shape adds these 9 cells (34.92-35.40 E, 32.46-33.03 N) and Philistia's shape loses them; the Samaria page, which says the kingdom controlled Samaria, Galilee and parts of Transjordan, names no coast and no year. Mirrors philistia /ledger/2 (reviewer fix).
c. 880 BCE: Samaria becomes the capital. The page has Samaria becoming the capital c. 880 BCE, where the House of Omri centred its rule in the 9th century.

region.text: Gilead and the Golan edge of northern Transjordan

ledger.note: 842 BCE (bridged): Hazael of Aram-Damascus presses Israel. The page says Hazael (reign 842–796 on the infobox) 'conquered Israel', with 'most of the Golan' in the Hazael-era expansion, but names no lands or years; Gilead is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Gilead and the Golan edge of northern Transjordan

ledger.note: 796 BCE (bridged): the contest ends with Hazael's reign (842–796); Israel's recovery followed Assyrian campaigns by Adad-nirari III (Samaria page) and Jeroboam II expanded the kingdom throughout northern Transjordan (793–753 or 786–746), no year.

region.text: Galilee (Naphtali) and the Gilead territories of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh

ledger.note: c. 732 BCE: Tiglath-Pileser III annexes Galilee and Gilead. The Samaria page has him annex Aram and the Gilead territories of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh and capture Naphtali (Galilee), placing an Assyrian governor over it, 'Around 732 BCE'. Hoshea's kingdom is the Samaria rump. The Tiglath-Pileser III page (fifth page) agrees on 732: Israel was defeated and divided, northern Israel became the province of Megiddo and southern Israel a vassal kingdom; in 733 Damascus was backed by Tyre, Ashkelon and Israel.

732 BCE: Israel is reduced to an Assyrian vassal kingdom. Tiglath-Pileser III 'defeated Israel, which he divided in half, annexing the northern portion of the kingdom as the province' of Megiddo and 'subjugating the southern portion as a vassal kingdom' (Tiglath-Pileser III page, reopened 2026-10-19; the year is the preceding sentence's 'In 732, Damascus fell'). Israel is the vassal and the Assyrian empire the suzerain; mirrors neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/16 (reviewer fix).

722 BCE: Samaria falls. 'Samaria I looked at, I captured; 27,280 men who dwelt in it I carried away', Sargon II recorded; Assyria besieged Samaria for three years, and the page dates the conquest to 722 BCE in one passage, c. 720 in others.
722 BCE: the Kingdom of Israel ends. Hoshea, the last king, is dated (732–c. 720 BCE); the infobox says conquered by Assyria c. 720. Cliopatria runs the shape to -701.

region.text: the Assyrian vassal kingdom of Samaria

ledger.note: 722 BCE: the vassal kingdom ends with the fall of Samaria (722 in one passage of the Samaria page, c. 720 in others); Assyria turns it into a province in the loss below. Mirrors neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/18.

wars.name: Israelite-Philistine wars

zones.text: the Philistine coastal plain and the border between them

wars.outcome: Saul died in battle against the Philistines; David defeated them and Philistia became a client state.
wars.note: No years on the page beyond the reigns (Saul 1047–1010, David 1008–970); the battles of Aphek, Eben-ezer, Gilboa and the Valley of Elah are on the Philistines page without years.

wars.name: Moabite revolt (Mesha Stele)
wars.outcome: The Mesha Stele, c. 840 BCE, records Moab's victory over Israel under King Mesha, against Omri and his son Ahab.
wars.note: The page does not say which lands Moab regained.

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar
wars.outcome: Ahab the Israelite and his ten thousand troops joined the anti-Assyrian coalition recorded on the Kurkh Monoliths (c. 853 BCE); no territory changed.
wars.note: The Samaria page does not name Qarqar; the Kurkh Monoliths mention 'Ahab the Israelite'.

wars.name: Aram-Damascus' conquest of Israel under Hazael
wars.outcome: Hazael 'conquered Israel'; Israel recovered after the Assyrian campaigns of Adad-nirari III.
wars.note: The page names no lands and no year for the conquest.

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Aram and northern Israel (Syro-Ephraimite War)
wars.outcome: Pekah of Israel and Rezin of Damascus threatened Ahaz of Judah, who appealed to Tiglath-Pileser III; he sacked Damascus and Israel and annexed Aram, Galilee and Gilead.
wars.note: The Aram-Damascus page dates the conflict only 'c. 732 BCE'.

wars.name: Siege of Samaria
wars.outcome: Assyria took Samaria after a three-year siege and carried off its people; Sargon II claimed the capture.
wars.note: -724 is computed from 'three years' ending in 722.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line survives for any border; the Judah frontier after 930, the Transjordan edge and the Aramean frontier are all approximate, and the united monarchy's extent is itself disputed (Finkelstein's Low Chronology).

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW: 'Kingdom of Israel' -1000..-701, 4 shapes, Wikipedia title '(united monarchy)'. The first shape (20,072 km2) is the united monarchy including the Judah core; Cliopatria keeps it to -901 although the division is c. 930 and starts the Kingdom of Judah only in -900 (new keyframe -930 cuts Judah out). The last shape runs 21 years past the fall of Samaria (722/c. 720): new keyframe -732 (the Samaria rump) and a dissolve at -722. A new keyframe -1047 covers Saul. ONE STATE: the dossier treats the united monarchy and the northern kingdom as one state (the Cliopatria row, one colour), with Judah as a `split` at -930; the Kingdom of Judah dossier (me-04, other part) takes the south. NOT DRAWN: Hazael's and Jeroboam II's changes in Transjordan (no years or lands on the pages) beyond a low-confidence contest over Gilead 842–796; Mesha's reconquest of Moab (c. 840); Omri's subjugation of Moab. Shiloh as the first capital (c. 1000–931 in the Samaria infobox) is not used because the united-monarchy page gives Gibeah, Mahanaim and Jerusalem. AREA: neither page has an infobox area. PAGE BUDGET: five pages (united monarchy, Samaria, Aram-Damascus, Jeroboam II, Tiglath-Pileser III). The rulers strip is omitted: the pages give reigns for Saul, Ish-bosheth, David, Solomon, Rehoboam, Jeroboam I, Jeroboam II and Hoshea only. COUNTERPARTS WANTED: moab, ammon, edom, aram-damascus (with Aram-Zobah), all vassal counterparts; the Neo-Assyrian dossier already records Israel as a vassal from 732 and the province Samerina in the 720s. FIX PASS 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): (1) Gibeah and Jerusalem: the -1047 shape and found region now include a 15 km Benjamin circle at Gibeah (the first version cut the whole Judah -900 area out, capital included); Mahanaim is kept to -1001 and Jerusalem starts at -1000 (the Kingdom of Israel (united monarchy) page, reopened, does not say David took Jerusalem). (2) Philistia: the -1047 shape no longer includes Philistia's -1150 strip; added gains from philistia at -1000 (10 cells, confidence 1) and -900 (9 coastal cells, confidence 1), mirroring philistia /ledger/1 and /2; the Judah-core gain at -1000 excludes the cells that come from philistia. (3) Added vassal_start (-732, confidence 3) and vassal_end (-722, confidence 2) by neo-assyrian-empire from the Tiglath-Pileser III page. Roles: in these two events and in the Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Edom and Aram events the counterpart string is the other party, and the vassal events in this ledger run both ways (Israel the suzerain of Philistia and the others, Israel the vassal of Assyria): every note says which. Not done (thin): Mesha's revolt (-840), Hazael's Gilead contest dating, a rulers strip.
